A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DatawiseAgent. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite extensive rewriting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DatawiseAgent evaluations on InfiAgent-DABench, MatplotBench, and DSBench, alongside ablations and a modeling case study.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and reports additional model-size robustness results and data-analysis costs.

M1.justification: The four-stage FST architecture and action choices remain unchanged. Published prompt specifications receive limited revisions: v2 Figure 10 adds an explicit current-user-instruction block, while Figures 12–13 omit debugging-trace preambles and placeholders present in v1 Figures 10–11. These establish changes to the documented prompting, without establishing associated experimental reruns.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate data analysis on InfiAgent-DABench, visualization on MatplotBench, and predictive modeling on DSBench. The new model-size experiments use existing task coverage; no additional dataset, domain, or input scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds TaskWeaver to the Qwen2.5-72B InfiAgent comparison, reporting 74.71% ABQ; the corresponding v1 comparison included only ReAct and AutoGen as baselines. Comparator membership in the visualization and predictive-modeling comparisons is retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds a systematic InfiAgent evaluation across Qwen2.5 models of 7B, 14B, 32B, and 72B parameters. It also revises the reported visual-tool allowance from five calls to four. InfiAgent is generally described as containing 257 cases instead of 258, although v2 Appendix D.2 still says 258; whether this reflects a correction or changed sample selection is unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds model-scale robustness analysis in Section 4.3/Figure 5 and extends cost-efficiency analysis to InfiAgent in Appendix A. It removes the markdown-removal ablation, 'w/o text,' from v1 Table 4. Planning and code-repair ablations remain; the earlier inference-time analysis and modeling case study are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark results. The case-study random_state=42 settings are retained, and the new model-scale figure also presents point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial model-scale and cost results: DatawiseAgent obtains 73.15%, 75.49%, and 81.71% ABQ with Qwen2.5-7B, 14B, and 32B, and InfiAgent costs are newly tabulated. Its Qwen2.5 visualization score changes from 56.61 to 56.41 in corresponding tables. The 'w/o text' results and ablation PASQ/UASQ entries disappear. Most existing benchmark scores, including DSBench results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.2 explicitly defines the FST six-tuple, input/output alphabets, and output-function mapping. v2 removes this detailed formalization while retaining the state space, transition description, algorithm, and diagrams. The evaluation-metric equations remain unchanged; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central notebook representation and FST contributions are retained. v2 expands the main claims to graceful degradation with smaller models and a widening advantage over baselines as model size decreases, extending v1's claims about adaptability across the three original model configurations.

C2.justification: v2 adds the hypothesis that a uniform cell representation reduces cognitive load and improves reasoning. Its new limitations section explicitly identifies single-tool evaluation and the absence of human-in-the-loop studies. Existing interpretations involving planning, code repair, and compensation for weaker models are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a code/data repository link, exact GPT model identifiers, and visual-tool pseudocode in Figure 9. These improve implementation and access documentation. Most transition limits, temperatures, hardware specifications, software versions, and the modeling timeout were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around AutoML and machine-learning agents, adding works such as DS-agent, AIDE, AutoKaggle, AutoML-agent, and MLCopilot. The discussion shifts from graph-maintenance overhead toward limited multi-turn interaction, task/model adaptability, and dependence on powerful proprietary models. Several earlier formalism and error-accumulation references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized from benchmark-specific sections into shared setup, effectiveness, robustness, and ablations. Appendices are reordered and subdivided, and limitations and ethics sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 condenses the main benchmark tables and places fuller versions in the appendices, adds score-gain columns, a model-scale plot, a cost table, and tool pseudocode. The inference-time plot is reformatted and moved into the main text. Prompt figures become larger styled code boxes; existing architecture diagrams and the case-study graphic are retained.

improvement.justification: The model-size study directly strengthens evidence for robustness, while new cost comparisons, implementation disclosures, explicit limitations, and clearer organization improve usefulness and transparency. These gains are moderated by removal of the text ablation and unresolved reporting inconsistencies, particularly the 257/258-case descriptions. Most core benchmark findings and the architecture remain stable, supporting a limited overall improvement.
